items.headline: Nasdaq has its worst day since June as the AI-spending trade wobbles
items.why: Doubts about financing costs and whether the AI capex boom has peaked hit the whole AI supply chain at once, and the semiconductor index only steadied Friday (+0.6%).

items.headline: Meta falls about 7% on AI-spending worries despite a revenue beat; Tesla cuts capex plans
items.why: The market is now punishing both camps, big spenders and companies cutting spend, so the AI-capex trajectory is the key variable for the Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon reports next week.

items.headline: Report that SpaceX is seeking thousands of cell sites for a fourth US wireless carrier hits AT&T and T-Mobile
items.why: A credible satellite-backed entrant moved incumbent carriers more than 6% in a day, while tower owner Crown Castle rose about 10%, so the market is pricing real competitive disruption.

items.headline: Bitcoin ends the week near $81,600, flat on the week after rejecting $84,000
items.why: Bitcoin has been trading in step with US equities, so its direction this week depends on the Fed meeting and the AI-stock earnings more than on anything crypto-specific.

items.why: Three straight weeks of ether fund outflows show institutional demand is fading even as the price holds around $2,400.
